papers.title: Conditional Diffusion for Multi-Agent TSN Scheduling

sections.Method: The scheduler adds Gaussian noise to a feasible schedule x0 during forward diffusion. A conditional denoiser reverses the process using traffic load and topology. The training objective combines noise-prediction MSE with a deadline-violation penalty.
sections.Experiments: On BurstTSN with 20, 50 and 100 flows, DiffTSN reduces deadline violations by 18 percent relative to PPO under bursty traffic.

papers.title: Graph Attention Actor-Critic for TSN Scheduling

sections.Method: A graph-attention encoder represents flow contention and an actor-critic policy selects scheduling actions directly. The method does not use iterative denoising.
sections.Experiments: The policy is fast at inference but its performance drops when the burst distribution differs from the training distribution.

papers.title: Robust TSN Scheduling under Dynamic Load

sections.Method: The controller optimizes a risk-sensitive objective and reports deadline violations, latency and schedule feasibility separately.
sections.Experiments: Robustness should be evaluated under distribution shift rather than only average latency on the training load.
